## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Taṇhāsaṁyojana Sutta* (Iti 15) is the fifteenth discourse of the *Itivuttaka*, situated in the *Ekakanipāta*. The sutta delivers a succinct teaching declaring that beings bound by the fetter of craving (*taṇhāsaṁyojana*) wander and transmigrate through the round of rebirth (*saṁsāra*) for an exceedingly long time. Together with its immediately preceding companion discourse, the *Avijjānīvaraṇa Sutta* (Iti 14), it highlights craving and ignorance (*avijjā*) as the fundamental twin obstacles in human existence, keeping beings bound such that they cannot transcend the wandering from existence to existence (*itthabhāvaññathābhāva*) [Pande 1974; Webster 2005].

  DharmaNexus also aligns this verse portion with canonical exegetical works such as the *Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa* (Cnd 23) and *Sāriputtasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 16), as well as commentary collections (*Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā* and *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā*), alongside cross-language verse alignments in the Sanskrit *Patna Dharmapada* [DharmaNexus].
